region: Watkins Glen · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Lakewood Vineyards has farmed the west shore of Seneca Lake, just north of Watkins Glen, since the Stamp family arrived at Lakewood Farm in 1951. For decades they grew grapes for juice companies and large wineries, then planted fine wine varieties in the 1980s and opened their own winery in 1989. Chris Stamp is the winemaker, his brother Dave runs about 100 acres of certified-sustainable vineyards, and a third generation is now at work. Chris’s father Monty was a founding member of the New York State Wine Grape Growers.

Lemberger is the German and old American name for the grape Austrians call Blaufränkisch, as Chris Stamp himself points out. It is a late-ripening, cold-hardy red that has found a real home in the Finger Lakes, where it makes bright, peppery wines with lively acidity rather than heavy ones. Lakewood’s version leans on that freshness: red and blue berries, a dash of white or cracked pepper, and a dry finish with a hint of spice. It suits the wood grill, from red meat to earthy mushrooms.
